\section[\texorpdfstring{\mw{बुणणो} (buṇṇo)}{बुणणो (buṇṇo)}]{\mw{बुणणो} (buṇṇo) — to weave}

\label{lesson:MW-C107-bunno}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Marwadi for to burn, then the Marwadi for to sew.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \mw{बुणणो}}
\textbf{\mw{बुणणो}} — \emph{buṇṇo} — \textquotedblleft{}to weave\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\mw{बुणणो}} (\emph{buṇṇo}) is a tadbhava, a word inherited and reshaped by sound change. It comes from \emph{*vināti}, \textquotedblleft{}weaves\textquotedblright{}, a form CDIAL reconstructs from its descendants. CDIAL lists Old Marwari \emph{bināi} under it (CDIAL 11773). Hindi \emph{bunnā} comes from the variant \emph{*vunāti}, as \textbf{\mw{बुणणो}} (\emph{buṇṇo}) does.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for this chapter.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{buṇṇo}, once more

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Marwadi for to burn, then the Marwadi for to sew, then say \emph{buṇṇo} again

\section[\texorpdfstring{\mw{रंगणो} (raṅgṇo)}{रंगणो (raṅgṇo)}]{\mw{रंगणो} (raṅgṇo) — to dye}

\label{lesson:MW-C107-rangno}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Marwadi for to sew, then the Marwadi for to weave.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \mw{रंगणो}}
\textbf{\mw{रंगणो}} — \emph{raṅgṇo} — \textquotedblleft{}to dye\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\mw{रंगणो}} (\emph{raṅgṇo}), \textquotedblleft{}to dye\textquotedblright{}, is the verb made from \emph{raṅg}, \textquotedblleft{}colour\textquotedblright{}. That word may come from Sanskrit \emph{raṅga}, \textquotedblleft{}dye, colour\textquotedblright{}, under which CDIAL lists Hindi \emph{rā̃g}, \textquotedblleft{}dye\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 10560), or from Persian \emph{rang}, \textquotedblleft{}colour\textquotedblright{}; the two may have merged.
\end{cousinweb}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\mw{लगावणो} (lagāvṇo)}{लगावणो (lagāvṇo)}]{\mw{लगावणो} (lagāvṇo) — to apply, to fix on}

\label{lesson:MW-C107-lagavno}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Marwadi for to weave, then the Marwadi for to dye.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \mw{लगावणो}}
\textbf{\mw{लगावणो}} — \emph{lagāvṇo} — \textquotedblleft{}to apply, to fix on\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\mw{लगावणो}} (\emph{lagāvṇo}) is a tadbhava, a word inherited from Sanskrit and reshaped by sound change. It comes from \emph{lagyati}, \textquotedblleft{}adheres to\textquotedblright{}. CDIAL lists Old Marwari \emph{lāgaï} under it (CDIAL 10895). It is the causing form of \emph{lāgṇo}, \textquotedblleft{}to stick, to seem\textquotedblright{}: \textquotedblleft{}make stick\textquotedblright{}, so \textquotedblleft{}apply\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}
